subject: Scheduling: Storix hands-on throughput preflight & test plan
messages:
From: Alice Kim <alice.kim@storix.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Eng Ops <eng+ops@storix.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Storix POC kickoff — hands-on throughput session request

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the team here at Storix is excited to move to a hands-on POC. We want to make sure the first working session focuses on throughput and routing so we can validate expected QPS and end-to-end latency. High-level asks:

- A 2-hour working session to run our load harness against a representative prompt set (we'll share).
- Verify routing behavior when traffic spikes (prefer graceful fallback to cheaper variants).
- Validate 99th percentile latency SLOs for 512-token responses.

Can your team run the session next week (preferred window: 29–31 Aug)? We can provide test credentials and an initial prompt file. I'm copying Eng Ops to coordinate slots.

Attaching a short requirements doc that summarizes the scenarios (storix_poc_requirements.pdf).

Regards,
Alice
Alice Kim
Director, Platform Engineering — Storix

Attachment: storix_poc_requirements.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Alice Kim <alice.kim@storix.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Storix POC kickoff — hands-on throughput session request

Thanks Alice — excited to run this. A few quick clarifying items before we lock a slot: 

1) Throughput targets: can you confirm target sustained QPS and burst QPS (e.g., 200 qps sustained, 500 qps burst)? Also indicate expected concurrency per prompt set.
2) Latency SLO: you mentioned 99th pct for 512 tokens — confirm the SLO target (e.g., 1.2s or 2.5s).
3) Test harness: do you need us to run Redwood's test harness (we can run the load generator from our environment) or will you run from Storix and point to our endpoints? Either works; preference is we run one controlled leg and Storix runs a cross-check.

My availability: 29 Aug 10:00–13:00 PT or 30 Aug 13:00–16:00 PT. Monica will own the runbook and routing configs; Vanessa will help with telemetry and SLO dashboards.

If those windows don't work, propose times and we'll reschedule. I'll draft a short test plan and attach it for review.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

--
Dylan is available via Slack: @dylan_b
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Alice Kim <alice.kim@storix.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Storix POC kickoff — hands-on throughput session request

Hi Alice and team — thanks for the requirements doc. I've attached a concise testplan that maps your scenarios to the harness steps and success criteria (redwood_throughput_testplan_v2.md). Key points from our side:

- We'll validate sustained QPS up to 250 and burst to 600 for short windows (30s bursts).
- Baseline latency SLO target: 99th <= 1.6s for 512-token responses using the recommended GPU profile. If Storix requires a tighter SLO we can try kernel and quantization adjustments but will note potential cost impact.
- We'll run two passes: (A) Redwood-controlled generator hitting a dedicated endpoint, (B) Storix-run cross-check to validate network variance.
- Routing: we'll enable a canary fallback policy that will route overflow to a lower-cost model family if queue depth exceeds threshold. We'll demonstrate the behavior in the session.

Proposed confirmed slot: 29 Aug 10:30–12:30 PT. If that works for Storix we'll send a calendar invite with prep notes and a short pre-run checkpoint 24h prior.

Attachment: redwood_throughput_testplan_v2.md

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Confirming: 29 Aug 10:00–12:00 PT is preferred. Please resend the invite with the new time and include a short pre-run checklist (network/firewall, credentials, expected endpoints).

Appreciate the flexibility — looking forward to the run.

Alice
